intro: If you've got business or sightseeing out on the Somdet District side of Kalasin and want a place that's easy to find on a main road, quiet, and fairly priced, Idin Place Hotel Somdet (Idin Place) comes up among locals passing through · It's a small hotel on the main road in Nong Wang Subdistrict, Somdet District · What guests consistently praise is that the rooms are spacious and clean, quiet, with generous free parking that fits cars and vans, and friendly staff, all at an affordable price · It's right on a main road, easy to find, on the Phu Phan side near Luang Pu Sila Dharma Park · From approx. ฿500/night · Real guest reviews say it's good value and peaceful, though it's a small hotel with no on-site restaurant, best suited to travellers with their own car.

body.html: Idin Place Hotel Somdet, or Idin Place, is a small hotel in Somdet District, Kalasin Province · It sits at 80 Moo 14, Nong Wang Subdistrict, Somdet District, right on the main road through town · This isn't a tall city hotel but a simple low-rise place with a garden around it, right on the road so it's easy to find and easy to get in and out of · It suits travellers with business around Somdet, people passing along the Kalasin–Mukdahan route, or anyone who wants to use it as a base for the Phu Phan side without staying in central Kalasin.

The appeal here is the rooms and the quiet · Reviews agree that the rooms are more spacious than you'd expect for the price, clean and quiet, so you sleep well · Rooms have air conditioning, a refrigerator, a TV and free Wi-Fi, with both non-smoking and smoking options · The front desk is open 24 hours, so check-in is easy even late at night, and there's daily housekeeping · Staff get praised for a warm, friendly welcome and for pointing guests to local eateries nearby.
"Clean, quiet hotel with spacious rooms and friendly staff, plenty of parking · Right on a main road, easy to find, good value for a stay around Somdet."

The overall feel is quiet and simple · The generous free parking is a favourite — it easily fits cars and vans, even with several vehicles · Because it's a small, simple hotel, the facilities are kept to the essentials rather than the full set of a big hotel — there's no swimming pool, and no on-site restaurant or breakfast · But the hotel does keep frozen food at reception that they'll heat up for you, and there are local eateries and convenience stores around Somdet, a short drive away for food.

The location is an advantage if you have a car and you're exploring the Phu Phan side · Somdet District is a gateway to the Phu Phan range, on the Kalasin–Sakon Nakhon/Mukdahan route · From here you can drive to Luang Pu Sila Dharma Park, a popular merit-making spot, along the same road, and it's near Somdet-area temples such as Wat Si Yaek Somdet · If you want to head into central Kalasin for the dinosaurs at the Sirindhorn Museum or the Lam Pao Dam, you can use this as a base and drive out · Being right on a main road makes coming and going easy, with no hunting through back lanes.

Honestly, from real reviews: the limitation here is that it's a small, simple hotel · There are a limited number of rooms, and no on-site restaurant or breakfast, so you'll need to plan your meals · It's out in Somdet District, a fair way from central Kalasin, so without a car it's awkward, as the food and sights are spread out and you'll need to drive or call a ride · Online reviews are still few, as it's a small hotel out in the district, so it's worth comparing prices and asking about room condition before you book · There's also a 100-baht key deposit, refunded at check-out.

In short, if you've got business or sightseeing on the Somdet side, have your own car, and want a quiet stay with spacious, clean rooms and easy free parking at a fair price, Idin Place Hotel Somdet is a sensible choice · The reviews capture it well: spacious, clean rooms, a quiet feel, friendly service and an easy-to-find location · The trade-off is that it's a small hotel with no on-site restaurant and you'll need a car · It suits travellers passing through, couples, small families and anyone wanting to stay on the Phu Phan side near Luang Pu Sila Dharma Park.

A tip from following the reviews here: book ahead, especially over long weekends, holidays and during merit-making events at Luang Pu Sila Dharma Park, since rooms are few and fill up fast · Ask for a non-smoking room when you book if you'd prefer one, and request a room set back from the road if you want extra quiet · And since there's no breakfast on site, grab something from the shops around Somdet beforehand, or use the heat-up service for the frozen food at reception.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Idin Place Hotel Somdet Kalasin

faq.q: Where is Idin Place Hotel Somdet, and what's nearby?
faq.a: Idin Place Hotel Somdet (Idin Place) is at 80 Moo 14, Nong Wang Subdistrict, Somdet District, Kalasin, right on the main road through the district, so it's easy to find · It's on the Phu Phan side, near Wat Si Yaek Somdet about 5 minutes' drive away, and on the route to Luang Pu Sila Dharma Park about 30 minutes' drive · Central Kalasin is about 45 minutes, while the Sirindhorn Museum (Phu Kum Khao dinosaurs) and the Lam Pao Dam are about an hour's drive.

faq.q: How much does Idin Place Hotel Somdet cost, and what rooms are available?
faq.a: Rates start at approx. ฿500/night for a Standard Double · A twin room and a non-smoking room run around ฿550–฿600 · It's a small hotel with a limited number of rooms, and prices vary by date, so compare Agoda and Trip.com or contact the property before booking · There's also a 100-baht key deposit, refunded at check-out.

faq.q: Who is Idin Place Hotel Somdet best for?
faq.a: It's best for anyone with business or sightseeing on the Somdet side, travellers passing through, couples and small families with their own car who want a quiet stay with spacious, clean rooms and easy free parking at a fair price · It's less suited to anyone who wants the full facilities of a big hotel, breakfast on site, or a central Kalasin stay where you can walk to food.

faq.q: Are the rooms clean, and is it quiet?
faq.a: Most reviews praise the spacious, clean and quiet rooms, so you sleep well · Every room has air conditioning, a refrigerator, a TV and free Wi-Fi, with both non-smoking and smoking options · Staff get praised for a warm, friendly welcome, and the front desk is open 24 hours so check-in is easy even late at night.

faq.q: Does Idin Place Hotel Somdet have a restaurant and breakfast?
faq.a: No, there's no on-site restaurant or breakfast · It's a simple hotel, so you should plan your meals — grab something from the shops around Somdet, or use the heat-up service for the frozen food at reception · There's generous free parking and a 24-hour front desk for convenience.

faq.q: Can I stay here without my own car?
faq.a: You can, but it's less convenient · The hotel is out in Somdet District, a fair way from central Kalasin, and food and sights are spread out, so you'll need to drive or call a ride · Without a car, rent one or arrange rides in advance and plan your meals · If you want to walk to food more easily, a central Kalasin stay would suit you better.
